clue.text: Where one gets to writing keenly at first in the USSR

definitions.text: Where one gets to writing keenly at first in the USSR

parts.note: taken as written
MS is the usual abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word keenly

explanation.surface: A traveller asks where in the Soviet Union one ends up by writing eagerly.
explanation.walkthrough: TO, then MS for a manuscript, then K from 'keenly at first' builds the name of a Siberian city, which the whole clue describes as a destination in the USSR.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomsk is a city in Siberia, part of the former Soviet Union, so it is a place one might travel to there.

clue.text: Excellent cricket score, say

definitions.meaning: early cricket scores were kept by cutting notches on a stick, so the best score is the top cut

explanation.surface: A fine total on the cricket field is praised as superb.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch is an idiom for first-rate, and literally a notch was an old cricket run, cut on a tally stick, so the highest such mark is a top one.

clue.text: Being low, dear, in France skulking around

definitions.note: the definition describes a person given to skulking, matching a noun

parts.note: lowing is the sound cattle make, so a moo is a cow being low
cher is the French word for dear

explanation.surface: A gloomy sweetheart on holiday in France slinks about miserably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being low' suggests feeling down; it is a cow's lowing.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch is to loiter or slink about idly, so a moocher is one who goes skulking around.

clue.text: Short measure

parts.note: a unit of weight whose usual name is the clipped form of a longer metric term

explanation.definitionFit: Kilo is the everyday shortening of kilogram, a unit of weight, so it is a measure that is itself abbreviated.

clue.text: Biblical character with a broken harp I observe

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into pieces, so the letters of harp are rearranged

parts.note: to observe is to see

explanation.surface: A figure from the Bible is spotted with a damaged harp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns HARP into PHAR, before I and SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharisees were a Jewish sect prominent in the New Testament, so one of them is a Bible figure.

clue.text: Re-knit better wool that it may be used for warmth

definitions.text: it may be used for warmth

indicators.note: knitting something again remakes the yarn into a fresh shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Knit the good wool again so it can keep someone warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Re-knit' signals rearranging BETTER WOOL THAT, fourteen letters, all of them fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber bottle filled from the kettle is placed in a bed to heat it.

clue.text: Spellbound in rewritten part

indicators.note: a passage that is rewritten is put down again differently, so the letters of part are reordered

explanation.surface: An actor is entranced by a role that has been revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' turns PART into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt describes someone wholly absorbed, as if under a spell.

clue.text: He tries to find a way to under write currency

indicators.note: in a down entry, writing one piece under another places the second below the first

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a river is a current, something that flows, a currency in its old sense

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to guarantee money by underwriting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under write' places RIVER beneath ST in the down light; 'currency' means flow, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: A striver is someone who makes efforts, so he is one who tries hard.

clue.text: Clear air thereabout

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters of there are rearranged

explanation.surface: The sky is clear somewhere near here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges THERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether is the poetic name for the clear upper sky, once thought to fill the heavens.

clue.text: Sharp practice could leave him with a sore throat

definitions.text: Sharp practice could leave him with a sore throat

parts.words: Sharp practice could leave him with a sore throat
parts.note: sharp practice reads as dishonesty but means training with blades pushed down the gullet

explanation.definitionFit: A fairground performer who pushes blades down his gullet would get a sore throat from practising.

clue.text: Clearly not one for the rich

definitions.text: Clearly not one for the rich

parts.words: Clearly not one for the rich
parts.note: a statute made for relief of the needy, plainly not aimed at the wealthy

explanation.definitionFit: The Poor Law was the old English system of relief for paupers, so it was plainly not legislation for wealthy people.

clue.text: Ruler who has to dry up

parts.note: taken as written
to parch is to dry up

explanation.surface: A leader who must fall silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry up' looks like forgetting one's lines; it is to parch.
explanation.definitionFit: A toparch was the governor of a small district or toparchy in the ancient world.

clue.text: Emperor found in the hot-house

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit inside the words the hot-house

explanation.surface: A ruler is discovered in the greenhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' picks letters across 'hot-house'.
explanation.definitionFit: Otho was a Roman emperor who reigned briefly in AD 69.

clue.text: Distress signal from George on a horse

indicators.note: on here sets the first piece ahead of the second, as a rider sits upon a mount

parts.note: George was the old phonetic-alphabet word for G
a roan is a horse with a coat flecked with white

explanation.surface: George, riding a horse, sends out a cry for help.
explanation.walkthrough: G stands for George in the old RAF phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A groan is a sound of pain or anguish, which signals suffering.

clue.text: One very cut off town in Bucks

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: cut off means a word loses its tail end, here the final letter of very

explanation.surface: A single, very isolated town in the English countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off' docks the Y of VERY. Bucks is Buckinghamshire, an English county west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Iver is a village in south Buckinghamshire, near Slough.

clue.text: Be an angel, you brute!

parts.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for saint, an angelic person

explanation.surface: A plea to be kind, addressed to a bully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angel' stands for a saint, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is a cruel or savage person, a synonym of brute.

clue.text: Flood caused by turning taps with energy

indicators.note: turning means the word taps is read the other way round

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Water pours out because someone turned on the taps vigorously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' turns TAPS into SPAT, then E.
explanation.definitionFit: A spate is a sudden rush of water in a river after rain.

clue.text: As precepts were devised for cleaners

indicators.note: devised means worked out afresh, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Rules were drawn up for domestic help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' rearranges AS PRECEPTS WERE, fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpet-sweepers are hand-pushed devices with rotating brushes for cleaning rugs.

clue.text: Frightful creature taking a fielding position on my right

parts.note: taken as written
mid-on is a cricket fielding position on the leg side near the bowler

explanation.surface: A fearsome beast stations itself in the field on my right.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-on is a cricket fielding position; in a down entry it comes after MY R.
explanation.definitionFit: A myrmidon is a ruthless henchman who carries out orders without scruple, a fearsome hired follower.

clue.text: Tiers of layers along the shore for protection?

parts.note: coastal means situated by the sea shore
a battery is a set of stacked cages for laying hens

explanation.surface: Rows of hens by the seaside are kept there for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layers' looks like strata; they are egg-laying hens, kept in a battery.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal battery is a group of guns sited to defend the shoreline against attack.

clue.text: Makes me reflexive, speaking regally

parts.note: the royal plural of myself, used by a monarch speaking of one person

explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign using the royal we says this form in place of myself, a reflexive pronoun.

clue.text: Butler's ideal nowhere to be found

indicators.note: to be found here means to be cast anew, as metal is founded, so the letters of nowhere are remade

explanation.surface: A manservant's perfect place cannot be located anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butler' is Samuel Butler, the novelist, not a servant; 'to be found' rearranges NOWHERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Butler's satirical novel describes an imagined utopian land of that name.

clue.text: Yorkshire banker with a keen resentment

parts.note: ire is sharp anger or resentment

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire financier who bears a bitter grudge.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' here is a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aire is a river flowing through Leeds in Yorkshire, and a river has banks.

clue.text: I join up with Father coming back, and get support

indicators.note: coming back means the joined pieces are read the other way round

parts.note: taken as written
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: Someone teams up with Dad on his return and finds backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns I UP PA round.
explanation.definitionFit: Appui is a word from French for a prop or point of stay, used of military positions and horsemanship.

clue.text: Arboreal deadly sinner?

parts.note: a tree-dwelling animal whose name is also one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.definitionFit: The slow tree-dwelling mammal shares its name with idleness, one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Crack from a seaman not articled

indicators.note: not articled means the word seaman drops an article, the two letters of an

explanation.surface: A wisecrack from a sailor who is not under contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articled' suggests being bound by a contract; here it means removing the article AN from SEAMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A seam is a narrow line or crack, as in a seam of coal or a split between boards.

clue.text: No-one's up in the Swiss town

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: NO plus I (one) plus S (from 's) gives these letters

explanation.surface: Nobody is awake in the Alpine town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NO, I and S in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Sion is the capital of the canton of Valais in Switzerland.

clue.text: An aching for French bread

definitions.meaning: an ache or hurt felt in the body
the French word for a loaf

explanation.surface: Someone is longing for a baguette.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means suffering in English and is the French word for loaf.

clue.text: Quietly criticise the show in advance

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for soft
to review is to give a critical assessment

explanation.surface: A critic quietly pans a performance before it opens.
explanation.definitionFit: A preview is a showing of a play or film before its official opening.

clue.text: Felt strongly carrying the burden around

indicators.note: carrying here means one word holds another within it
around confirms that the burden goes about the word the

parts.note: a load is a burden

explanation.surface: Someone bearing a heavy load had strong feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathed means hated intensely, a strong emotion felt toward something.

clue.text: What's afoot in the Forces

parts.note: afoot reads as happening but means the troops who march on foot

explanation.definitionFit: Foot soldiers form the branch of an army that fights on foot.

clue.text: No inn? Strange -that's a fabrication!

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of order, so the letters of no inn are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller finds no inn and suspects the story is a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a fabrication' means a fabric, not a lie; 'Strange' rearranges NO INN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a sheer lightweight silk or voile fabric.
